goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — SQL injection: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` interpolates admin-writable site-setting text unescaped; a crafted legacy host value executes arbitrary SQL as the migration role during deploy. Use quote()/binds

adjudication.rationale: The migration builds a raw SQL string with `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"` where `h` comes from `site_settings.value` for `embeddable_hosts` (previously an admin-configurable setting). Because `h` is interpolated directly into SQL without quoting/escaping or binds, a value containing a `'` will at minimum break the migration, and a crafted value could inject additional SQL executed with the migration’s DB privileges. This is directly verifiable in the diff at db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:15 — same unguarded `[0]['value']` for `uncategorized_category_id`; that row exists only if explicitly set, so the fallback path also crashes

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does `execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value'].to_i` with no check that the query returned any rows. If `site_settings` does not contain a persisted row for `uncategorized_category_id` (e.g., if defaults aren’t stored in the table), `[0]` will be `nil` and the migration will crash (`NoMethodError` on `[]`). The same unguarded pattern also exists for the earlier `embed_category` lookup. So the finding points to a real, verifiable crash risk in the diff (though whether the row exists in all deployments depends on how `site_settings` is populated).

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3 — `create_table ... force: true` silently drops an existing `embeddable_hosts` table and its data

adjudication.rationale: The migration explicitly calls `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, and in Rails this `force: true` option will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it. That is a real, verifiable data-loss risk if an `embeddable_hosts` table exists for any reason (e.g., previously created manually, a failed/partial migration rerun, or divergent schema in an existing install).

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:2 — `def change` containing `execute`/`DELETE` is irreversible (IrreversibleMigration); should be `def up`, and it deletes the only copy of the source settings

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` uses `def change` but performs raw `execute` SQL inserts/selects and a `DELETE FROM site_settings ...`. Rails cannot automatically infer how to reverse these operations, so rolling back this migration would raise `ActiveRecord::IrreversibleMigration` unless explicit `up/down` (or `reversible`) logic is provided. Additionally, it deletes the original `site_settings` rows for `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` after copying, so a failed/partial migration would remove the source data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — non-sargable predicate with no functional index on `lower(host)`: every embed request full-scans the table; `.first` on a non-unique column also makes the chosen category arbitrary

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, which queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`. The migration `create_embeddable_hosts` does not add any index on `host` (nor an expression index on `lower(host)`), so this lookup cannot use an index and will require scanning rows as the table grows. Also, there is no uniqueness validation or DB unique constraint on `host`, so duplicates are possible; using `.first` means the returned record/category would be whichever row the DB happens to return first, making the chosen category effectively arbitrary in that case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3 — no index on `host`, no UNIQUE on `host`, no FK on `category_id` despite `null: false`; orphaned category_ids and duplicate hosts are representable

adjudication.rationale: The migration `create_embeddable_hosts` creates `embeddable_hosts` with `host` and `category_id` but does not add any DB-level constraints or indexes. This is directly verifiable in the diff: no `add_index` on `host` (even though runtime code frequently looks up by host via `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`), no UNIQUE constraint/index on `host` (so duplicate allowed-host rows are representable, making `record_for_host(...).first` ambiguous), and no foreign key on `category_id` despite `null: false` and a `belongs_to :category` association (so orphaned `category_id` values are representable at the DB layer if categories are deleted or data is inserted outside app validations).

In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, the `update` action (triggered by `PUT /admin/customize/embedding` per `config/routes.rb`) does not read any params or modify any persisted state; it just re-renders the current `@embedding` OpenStruct via `render_serialized`. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6:5 — `saveChanges` is unreachable dead code (embedding.hbs renders no save button), and would hit the no-op server action anyway

adjudication.rationale: In the new `admin/templates/embedding.hbs`, the only top-level action wired is `addHost` (plus per-row component actions like `save`/`delete`). There is no `{{d-button ... action="saveChanges"}}` (or other reference) to trigger `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6`’s `saveChanges` action, so within this diff it is unused/unreachable from the UI. Additionally, the corresponding server endpoint `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` just re-renders the serializer and performs no persistence, and the client calls `embedding.update({})` with an empty payload, making it a no-op even if invoked.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:10,15 — `where(id:).first` used unguarded in `update` and `destroy`; unknown/stale id yields nil → NoMethodError 500 instead of 404
matched_golden_ids: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `EmbeddableHost.where(id:).first` is used without checking for nil in the `update` and `destroy` actions, and that a missing/stale ID would yield nil and lead to a NoMethodError (500) rather than handling it (e.g., 404). This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:23 — `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` with no `require`/`permit`; a request missing the wrapper key raises NoMethodError → 500. Should be `params.require(:embeddable_host).permit(:host, :category_id)`

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, the code directly dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]`. If a client sends a malformed request missing the `embeddable_host` wrapper key (or it’s nil), this will evaluate `nil[:host]` and raise `NoMethodError`, resulting in a 500. This is a concrete failure mode present in the diff. Using `params.require(:embeddable_host)` (and optionally `permit`) would avoid that class of error and return a 400 instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:25 — silently substitutes `uncategorized_category_id` when no category is sent, so the stored row can disagree with the admin's selection; `category_id` existence is never validated (no FK, no presence validation)

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, `host.category_id` is assigned directly from `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` and only falls back to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` when it is blank. There is no validation in `EmbeddableHost` (only a `belongs_to :category`) ensuring the referenced category actually exists, and the migration adds no foreign key constraint—so an arbitrary/nonexistent `category_id` can be persisted. The “silent substitution” behavior is also present (blank category becomes uncategorized) though whether that disagrees with an admin’s selection depends on client behavior; the lack of existence validation/constraint is the clearly verifiable integrity issue in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:5 — check-then-insert with no unique index: concurrent creates for the same host both succeed, producing duplicates resolved arbitrarily by `record_for_host`

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbeddableHost` records used for authorization via `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, which does `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`. The new migration `create_embeddable_hosts` creates the table without any unique index/constraint on `host`, and the model has no `validates_uniqueness_of :host` either. The admin controller `create` blindly saves a new record (`save_host(EmbeddableHost.new)`) with no de-duplication. As a result, duplicate rows for the same host can be created (including via concurrent requests), and `record_for_host` will return an arbitrary “first” match, which is a real correctness issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — validation permits `:port` and a path, but normalization strips only scheme/path and `record_for_host` compares against `uri.host` (no port); a host saved with a port is permanently unmatchable

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. `EmbeddableHost` allows storing hosts with an optional port via the regex on `host` (e.g. `example.com:3000`). The `before_validation` normalization strips scheme and any path but does not remove a `:port`, so `host` can be persisted with a port. However `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL and uses `uri.host` (which excludes the port) and then queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. That will never match a stored value like `example.com:3000`, making such records effectively unusable for `host_allowed?` checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:12 — `record_for_host` returns `false`, `nil`, or a record — three-valued return; callers (`eh.try(:category_id)`) work by accident

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, early exits return `false`, while the final query returns an AR record or `nil`. This is inconsistent, but in the diff all shown callers treat falsy values equivalently: `host_allowed?` uses `.present?` (false/nil both yield false), and `TopicEmbed.import` uses `eh.try(:category_id)` (ActiveSupport `try` on `false` safely returns nil). So there’s no verifiable bug introduced here—at worst it’s an API consistency/style concern, not a defect evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:10 — exact-string matching only; `www.example.com` vs `example.com` are unrelated with no UI hint

adjudication.rationale: `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` parses the URL and then does `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, so `www.example.com` and `example.com` will not match unless both are explicitly stored. However, this is not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff: exact-host whitelisting is a reasonable/intentional policy (and the prior `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` implementation also relied on exact host equality). The “no UI hint” part is subjective and not provably incorrect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:43 — `category: eh.try(:category_id)` passes an integer id where the previous value (`SiteSetting.embed_category`) was a category *name* string (confirmed by the migration's `s.value = c.name` join); unless PostCreator accepts ids, embedded topics silently land in the default category. Untested

However, whether this is a bug depends on `PostCreator`’s accepted input types, which is not shown in the diff. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic.rb:869 — `expandable_first_post?` drops the "embedding configured at all" guard with no `EmbeddableHost.exists?` replacement; first posts stay expandable on sites with zero hosts

app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:38 — sets `category` from local `categoryId` rather than the save response; for a newly added host `edit()` never ran so `categoryId` is null, the server stores uncategorized, and the row shows an empty badge until reload

app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:20 — `cantSave` guards only the host string; saving with no category chosen is allowed and silently falls back to uncategorized, contradicting the explicit-mapping intent

adjudication.rationale: In `embeddable-host.js.es6`, `cantSave` only checks `buffered.host` (and `isSaving`), so a new host can be saved with `categoryId === null`. However, the server-side controller (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`) explicitly treats a blank `category_id` as valid input and assigns `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` when `host.category_id.blank?`. Given `category_id` is `null: false` in the migration, this fallback appears intentional to ensure a valid category even when none is chosen in the UI. adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:153 — `resources :embeddable_hosts` generates index/show/new/edit routes the controller doesn't implement (ActionNotFound); should be `only: [:create, :update, :destroy]`

adjudication.rationale: In config/routes.rb the diff adds `resources :embeddable_hosts, constraints: AdminConstraint.new`, which generates the full RESTful set of routes (index/show/new/edit/create/update/destroy). The new `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` in the diff only defines `create`, `update`, and `destroy` (no `index`, `show`, `new`, or `edit`). Any request to the generated GET routes (e.g., `/admin/embeddable_hosts` or `/admin/embeddable_hosts/:id`) would match a route but raise `AbstractController::ActionNotFound` because the action is missing. Constraining the routes with `only: [:create, :update, :destroy]` would avoid this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:16 — `OpenStruct` used with no `require 'ostruct'`; relies on a transitive require

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `OpenStruct.new` in `Admin::EmbeddingController#fetch_embedding`, but whether this will raise `NameError` depends on the broader app boot process (Rails or other files may already `require 'ostruct'`). adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:192 — `_hydrateEmbedded` now matches every `*_ids` key on every model type globally, to serve the single new `embed: :ids` serializer
app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:197 — plural branch calls `obj[k].map` with no array/null guard; any scalar or null `*_ids` attribute on any store-loaded model now throws

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural branch is entered for any key matching `/(.+)_id(s?)$/` where the optional `s` is present (i.e. `*_ids`). That branch unconditionally does `obj[k].map(...)`. If the API payload contains `some_ids: null`/`undefined` (or any non-array scalar) this will raise `TypeError: obj[k].map is not a function` during hydration. The subsequent `hydrated || []` does not prevent this, because the exception occurs before `hydrated` is assigned. This is a real correctness hazard introduced by the diff, even though the new embedding serializer likely emits arrays.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:201 — plural branch deletes the `*_ids` key unconditionally even when nothing hydrated (singular branch deletes only on success), silently dropping raw id data for all models

adjudication.rationale:
In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6, _hydrateEmbedded was changed to handle keys matching /(.+)\_id(s?)$/. In the plural "*_ids" branch, it always does:
- `const hydrated = obj[k].map(...)` (which always returns an array, even if every lookup returns null/undefined)
- assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` (the `|| []` is ineffective because `hydrated` is always truthy)
- **unconditionally** `delete obj[k]`

By contrast, the singular "*_id" branch only deletes the raw id key when `hydrated` is truthy. So for payloads where the ids cannot be hydrated (e.g., missing/filtered sideloaded records), this change will drop the original `*_ids` array and replace it with an array of null/undefined entries, losing the raw id data. That is a real correctness regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:200 — `hydrated || []` is dead code (`Array.prototype.map` never returns falsy); unresolvable ids become `undefined` entries the UI then renders

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural-ids branch does `const hydrated = obj[k].map(id => self._lookupSubType(...))` and then assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []`. Since `Array.prototype.map` always returns an Array (truthy) when it runs, `|| []` is effectively unreachable/redundant. More importantly, if `_lookupSubType` can’t resolve an id it will return `undefined` (or falsy) and the `map` will preserve that as an `undefined` element in the resulting array; unlike the singular `_id` case, there is no guard/filtering, and the code also deletes the original `*_ids` field unconditionally. That is a real correctness risk introduced by this diff (undefined entries in hydrated relations).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6:22 — `type.replace('_', '-')` (string pattern, not `/_/g`) replaces only the first underscore, so any future multi-underscore admin model silently misses the `/admin/` base path

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the only admin models involved are `plugin`, `site-customization` (from `site_customization`), and `embeddable-host` (from `embeddable_host`). Each requires at most a single underscore-to-dash conversion, so `type.replace('_', '-')` works correctly for all cases shown/introduced here. The finding is about hypothetical “future multi-underscore admin model” behavior, which is not a verifiable defect demonstrated by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:153 — `resources :embeddable_hosts` sits outside the `scope "/customize"` block while the singleton lives at `customize/embedding`; one feature split across two URL namespaces, papered over by the hardcoded `pathFor` in admin/adapters/embedding.js.es6:4
